title: Tsarist Reform and Reaction 1855-1917

walkthroughs.body_html: Defeat in the Crimean War (1856) exposed Russia's backwardness. The Emancipation Edict of 19 February 1861 freed the serfs but tied them to communal redemption payments lasting 49 years. The zemstva (1864), the judicial reform (1864) and military service reform (1874) followed. Reaction grew after Karakozov's attempt on the Tsar's life (1866); Alexander II was assassinated by the People's Will on 1 March 1881.

Sergei Witte (Finance Minister 1892-1903) drove rapid industrialisation: the gold standard (1897), foreign loans, the Trans-Siberian Railway (1891-1916). Industrial output doubled in the 1890s, but at the cost of an urban proletariat and rural taxation that depressed living standards.

Defeat in the Russo-Japanese War (1904-05) was followed by Bloody Sunday (22 January 1905): roughly 200 killed. A general strike and the formation of the St Petersburg Soviet forced the October Manifesto (17 October 1905). The Fundamental Laws (April 1906) curtailed the Duma's powers. Stolypin combined agrarian reform with the 'Stolypin necktie' of field-court hangings until his assassination in 1911.

mcqs.q: In what month and year were the serfs emancipated?
options: February 1861
March 1881
October 1905
February 1917

mcqs.q: What name was given to the local councils created in 1864?
options: Zemstva
Soviets
Dumas
Mirs
The 1905 Revolution achieved nothing because the Tsar stayed in power.
It failed to overthrow the Tsar but forced the October Manifesto creating the Duma, exposing autocracy's weaknesses and rehearsing the structures of 1917.
The 1905 Revolution was led by Lenin from the Winter Palace.
The October Revolution overthrew the Tsar.

mcqs.q: Why did the Provisional Government fail in 1917?
options: The Provisional Government fell because the Tsar returned and reclaimed his throne.
The Provisional Government fell because Lenin was personally more charismatic than Kerensky.
The October Revolution overthrew the Tsar.
It continued the unpopular war, did not redistribute land, shared 'dual power' with the Petrograd Soviet, and was discredited by the Kornilov affair before the Bolshevik takeover.

mcqs.q: How did the Bolsheviks seize power in October 1917?
options: Trotsky's Military Revolutionary Committee coordinated a near-bloodless takeover of key buildings in Petrograd from a Provisional Government that had lost army and worker support.
The October Revolution overthrew the Tsar.
The October Revolution was a mass popular uprising that stormed the Winter Palace.
The Provisional Government fell because the Tsar returned and reclaimed his throne.
